findings.message: At 100 bp per bin, 22.5% of called bins are heterozygous (K), which implies 2.54 heterozygous sites per kb and about 12.1% of K bins holding two or more of them (more if heterozygosity varies along the genome). PSMC only sees whether a bin holds one, so the oldest part of the curve loses resolution.
findings.recommendation: Re-bin the per-site data at 40 bp per bin or less, the largest size that keeps the share below 5.0% at this heterozygosity: `--bin-size 40` for VCF and multihetsep input, or `fq2psmcfa -s 40` for a psmcfa file, which psmc-rs then reads with `--bin-size 40` so that the results are scaled with the same bin size.

findings.message: 50.2% of bins lie in 877 sequences shorter than the bootstrap trunk (500,000 bins), which the bootstrap can only resample whole.
findings.recommendation: For the bootstrap, a trunk of at most 176,763 bins keeps at least 80.0% of bins in sequences of one trunk or more (--bootstrap-block-size).

findings.message: 15 of 87 sequences with at least 1.00 Mb in called bins have a heterozygosity far from their median of 2.90 per kb (more than 5 MADs of log theta and 1.5-fold): ML679952.1 (0x), ML679949.1 (0.00040x), ML679950.1 (0.00071x), ML681653.1 (0.00072x), ML681645.1 (0.00083x), ML679951.1 (0.0013x), ML679965.1 (0.0061x), ML679957.1 (0.015x), ML680145.1 (0.035x), ML679988.1 (0.046x) and 5 more.
findings.recommendation: High heterozygosity can come from contamination, collapsed duplications or copy-number variants, or reference errors; low heterozygosity from sex-linked scaffolds (near zero when hemizygous), runs of homozygosity (inbreeding, a real signal), deletions or an over-strict mask. Check depth, mapping quality, the mask and the chromosome assignment of these sequences, and exclude any that are artefacts or hemizygous.
